title: decompose-enqueue-pipeline-and-introduce-lease-arbitration-with-kv-warmup-shim
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Decompose the current monolithic enqueue and batch coordination path into an explicit stage pipeline (Ingress → Admission → Coalescer → Prefetch → Slot Allocator → Commit). Replace the single global scheduler lock with a lease-based slot arbitration system that respects NUMA/locality hints and soft backpressure tokens. Introduce a small, pluggable KV warmup shim that pre-populates hot prefixes asynchronously before a slot is committed.

Why: Over time the enqueue path has accreted special-case fast paths and a global scheduler that serializes many decisions. This causes contention at high concurrency, KV-cache thrashing for newly admitted sessions, and unpredictable tail latencies during bursts. The goal is to reduce contention, improve cache priming for hot keys, and give clearer boundaries for future optimizations (e.g., remote-prefetch and admission-cost accounting).

Design approach:
- Split the pipeline into explicit stages with well-defined handoff contracts and backpressure tokens. Each stage lives in its own bounded queue with metrics on queue length, age, and dropped frames.
- Implement Lease-based Slot Arbitration: instead of a global lock, slot owners acquire time-bound leases for contiguous slot ranges. Leases include locality and preferred-GPU hints to optimize KV locality and kernel selection.
- KV Warmup Shim: a pluggable worker that accepts (session_id, prefix_range, priority_hint) and issues async prefetches into the KV cache. The shim exposes a simple contract: warmup(session, deadline) -> best-effort ready/no-ready signal.
- Admission scoring: lightweight estimator for expected token length + model affinity; used to decide whether to admit, queue, or reject under overload.
- Feature-flagged rollout: default path remains the existing enqueue; new pipeline enabled behind runtime.feature_decompose_enqueue. Start with shadow mode, then canary, then full rollout.

Performance targets (bench):
- 95th-percentile tail latency under steady load: reduce by >= 15%.
- Relative token cost for same throughput: <= 5% regression.
- KV miss amplification (misses per session start) reduced by >= 25% for hot prefixes.

Migration considerations:
- Gracefully handle in-flight sessions: existing sessions continue on legacy path until completion; new sessions opt into the pipeline when feature flag on.
- Provide a migration audit trace and a CLI to list sessions in each path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit-tests covering lease acquisition/release and lease-extension failure paths.
- Integration test harness that emulates bursty arrivals and validates tail latency improvement and KV warmup hits.
- Benchmark results comparing baseline vs new pipeline (script checked into tools/bench/ENG-147258-runner).
- Dashboard panels added to Console telemetry: pipeline stage latencies, lease acquisition histogram, kv-warmup success rate, admission rejections.
- Documentation PR with rollout checklist, rollback plan, and observed benchmarks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect lease release could lead to slot starvation: add watchdog that auto-reclaims expired leases and logs diagnostic dumps.
- KV warmup could increase noise and evict other hot items: warmup is rate-limited and exposes a priority hint to avoid eviction storms.
- Scheduler correctness under partial deployment: maintain legacy compatibility and run cross-path consistency checks during canary.
